scope: Static bytecode metrics for the complete named methods in the already-built qualified before/after JDT JARs. No product compilation or test execution.

analysisTool.onlyChange: Method-name selection changed to decodeCodeAttribute, digit, inlineTagCompletion. Counting logic unchanged.
analysisTool.analysisExecution: JDK25 source-file launcher; analysis reader compiled in memory only.

definitions.instructions: Count of JVM Instruction elements in the complete method Code attribute, including every control-flow path.
definitions.codeBytes: CodeAttribute.codeLength: encoded JVM instruction array bytes; excludes constant pool, exception table, other metadata, classfile/container overhead and JIT machine code.
definitions.branches: BranchInstruction plus LookupSwitchInstruction/TableSwitchInstruction sites; a switch counts as one site, not its number of targets.
definitions.callSites: InvokeInstruction and InvokeDynamicInstruction sites, including constructors; static sites, not executed call counts.
definitions.allocations: Explicit new/newarray/anewarray/multianewarray sites; excludes allocations inside called methods and any runtime/JIT elimination.
definitions.maxStack: Code attribute max_stack in JVM operand-stack slots, not peak heap consumption.
definitions.maxLocals: Code attribute max_locals in JVM local-variable slots.

findings: ScannerHelper removes four instructions and six encoded bytes; its branch/call/allocation sites and maxStack are unchanged.
CompletionEngine removes four instructions and four encoded bytes; its branch/call/allocation sites and maxStack are unchanged.
MethodInfo adds 108 instructions and 261 encoded bytes, ten branch sites, 29 call sites and eight explicit allocation sites; maxStack remains 5, maxLocals rises from 9 to 11.

MethodInfo contains the original-loop fallback plus the 4096-iteration crossover and a BigInteger closed-form path, so a source-level loop optimization produces a substantially larger complete method.

No conclusion about runtime speed, executed instructions, measured allocation volume or JIT machine-code size follows from these static counts. BigInteger methods can allocate beyond the eight explicit new sites counted here.
